messages:
alisa: Heads-up — we've had a request to onboard a community release called 'horizon-5b-open-v2'. Need a quick licensing triage + quantization smoke plan before we start evals. pinging legal and infra.

sam_legal: Thanks. First thing — do we have the canonical license link? any non-commercial / hosting-prohibited language?

alisa: Repo points to 'Horizon Public License v1.0' in repo root. There's a weird clause about 'hosting commercial inference services' and a derivative redistribution section that mentions 'models converted for distribution require explicit permission'. Link: https://repo.example/horizon-5b-open-v2/LICENSE

mohit: If hosting is restricted we should avoid exposing it on Redwood API. Dedicated/Private OK maybe. Need exact prohibition text.

dana_research: From ML side: we usually quantize (4-bit / 8-bit) and produce derivative artifacts. If license forbids 'derivative distribution' that could block providing quantized weights to customers. Also we need to check export-control (crypto-like) flags.

sam_legal: I'll grab the license text and annotate sections. Quick checklist I'm proposing: 1) full license text capture + owner contact, 2) clear answer on commercial hosting, 3) permission for weight modifications (quantization / pruning), 4) redistribution rules (can we redistribute quantized weights to customers?), 5) export control / jurisdiction red flags, 6) attribution / model card obligations. I'll own 1/3/5.

jen_ops: For bring-up we should run a two-track plan in parallel: legal triage + technical smoke. Tech smoke steps: - small float inference (sanity), - post-quant accuracy checks on key eval sets, - perf/latency on Dedicated GPU, - run model-validator harness for safety/toxicity quick checks. I can spin up a dedicated node for smoke tests.

dana_research: Here's a tiny eval snippet we can run quickly on a small eval shard:

```
# quick eval harness
from model_harness import load_model, evaluate
m = load_model('horizon-5b-open-v2', dtype='float32')
base = evaluate(m, 'redwood-smoke/qc-1000')
q = m.quantize('bits=4')
qres = evaluate(q, 'redwood-smoke/qc-1000')
print('base', base['accuracy'], 'quant', qres['accuracy'])
```

This gives a fast regression signal. We'll tag the results and attach to the intake ticket.

license-bot: automated-scan: POSSIBLE_RESTRICTION match on license text: "hosting commercial inference services". Recommend legal review.

sam_legal: Confirmed — clause 7.2 reads: "Models and resulting derivatives may not be hosted by third parties for commercial inference services without express written permission of the rights holder." That blocks us offering it on Redwood API or sharing quantized weights to customers. Private/Dedicated where customer owns hardware may be OK but needs contractual review.

mohit: OK useful. For experiments we can do local quantization and internal evaluations (no distribution). Can we keep artifacts internal-only, and label model catalog entry as 'no-hosting, internal-eval-only' ?

sam_legal: Yes, that label is the right immediate mitigation. Also recommend outreach to upstream: ask for a commercial license or permission to redistribute quantized weights. I'll draft the outreach email today.

jen_ops: Action items from ops/eng: - tag catalog: "restrict-hosting" (jen) - run float + 4-bit smoke (dana/mohit) - avoid publishing weights outside Redwood (mohit) - create a short readme for SEs about limitations (alisa)

dana_research: Running smoke now on a small shard. I'll post initial numbers in this thread in ~2h. If quant drop >2% on our key metrics we should escalate to quality gate.

alisa: Thanks. For prioritization: this model came from a partner pilot but legal restriction means lower product priority until permission granted. Marking as "on-hold: licensing" in the intake board.

mohit: Quick note on export/control: model originates in Entity X (jurisdiction Y) — if there are sanctions flags we need export check; sam, can you confirm that in your review?

sam_legal: Will include jurisdiction & export in my write-up. If there's a sanctions list hit, the whole onboarding is blocked pending legal.

license-bot: note: outreach ticket created -> #LIC-2026 (sam_legal assigned)

alisa: Perfect — owners and ETAs: sam (legal) by EOD+2, dana/mohit (tech smoke) by EOD+1, jen (catalog tag + ops readme) by EOD+1. We'll reconvene in this thread when smoke results and legal note are in. :thumbsup:

jen_ops: Copy. :white_check_mark:

mohit: quick status: quant smoke started, ETA ~45m.

dana_research: initial smoke results: base perplexity 21.4, 4-bit quant perplexity 22.0, MMLU delta -0.9. Within our quick tolerance but legal constraint remains. attaching small CSV to the intake ticket.

alisa: Good, keeping this logged. Final decision: do NOT list on Redwood hosted API, allowed for internal evals and Private/Dedicated with contractual signoff. Sam will escalate licensing outreach. Closing triage until legal returns.

sam_legal: On it, will post reply when I hear back from upstream.

license-bot: thread-flag: triage-complete (pending upstream reply)
